title: From parabolic wavefront windows to generalized singular rays
reviewed_arguments: All 20 original obligations, 18 displays, 17 labelled equations, both complete solutions and original figure coordinates remain. Existing proofs and alternative routes are retained.

The characteristic normal form and gliding field use the current U053 convention. The analytic window premise retains compact uniformity, both time directions, the characteristic restriction and both width inequalities.
The full smooth-flow provider gives a common compact collar and parameter bounds. Oriented FTC integration proves the AM t squared/2 remainder for both time signs.

Contraposition with epsilon=L|t| supplies nonempty characteristic fibers for every anchor and small time. The declared choice input allows arbitrary selections without continuity. All time cutoffs yield the strict target-error bound.
Conservation of R0 under its Hamilton flow and the two mean-value bounds give rho squared at most 2BL t squared. Both normal roots are controlled without a sign selection.

Center changes and positive time rescaling are justified by their common first-order velocity and uniform Taylor remainders. The actual cosphere transfer uses lambda=|eta|, independent of normal momentum; conic-set invariance is explicit.

Hamilton homogeneity proves the normalized field descends to the cosphere. Its reduced flow and projected old center agree to quadratic order. A normal O(t) error is never silently treated as quadratic.

The conditional theorem applies the complete U053 closed-set trajectory proof with every compact tangency, ordinary/reflected/diffractive invariance and clock hypothesis. It keeps maximal two-sided continuation and escape, without adding uniqueness.

Relative closedness is taken in the open region excluding forcing wavefront. Analytic window regularity, boundary-data reduction and characteristic containment remain explicit later PDE obligations, not consequences of this geometric proof.

The corrected Vasy threshold is checked by the complete scalar inequality giving 5c0/16>c0/4. Fixed large L makes epsilon=L delta a quadratic window while every fixed-width source remainder is retained.

The first exercise checks all rational thresholds and both signs. The second retains the exact homogeneous principal-type symbol, infinite contact, nonzero clock and a closed sloping set with linear-window witnesses but no generalized arc.

The completed-square distance identity proves the quadratic window fails for that counterexample. The exact original figure keeps the same coordinate scale and all points; long legend lines now fit the canvas.

Melrose-Sjostrand has Definition 1.2 and Lemma 1.3; the citation is corrected. Lebeau Proposition VII.1 is an analytic wave result, and Vasy Proposition 7.3 must be read with its full correction. Their external prerequisites are not imported as programme proofs.
later_scope_not_claimed: General PDE window regularity and full source/Sobolev estimates
